name: moment
title: Moment
description: The game speaking in the stream: an eyebrow, a headline, one line of body and one action, posted by a host or by a live feed. It is the only thing in a stream carrying a button, which is the point of the component rather than a detail of it, because a room where three cards each offer a different button is a menu and not a conversation. It settles in place: give it a `result` and the same card becomes the answer, the action goes and the split bar arrives, and no second card is posted underneath. One rule with two reasons. A stream carrying a question card and a result card carries two answers to one question, and the second card would arrive in flow and push what the reader is looking at. It settles nothing itself: the share, the summary and the words are the host's, because only the host knows what the room answered.
docs: Render one into the stream as a child of `chat-stream`, alongside the messages. Give it `action` while the round is open and `result` when it closes; passing `result` to the card that is already there is the whole design, and posting a second `moment` for the answer is the thing this component exists to stop. `result.share` is what share of the room got it right, nought to a hundred, drawn as the bar and as the figure: a number outside that range is clamped rather than drawn past its own track. `result.summary` is a node, because the sentence under the bar counts people and names the reader, and neither is the library's to word. `result.eyebrow` overrides the library's own word for a settled card. A moment with no `action` is an announcement and draws no button, which is the only supported way to have none.
